dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI & test-suite orientation

evidence.note: Read run_tests.sh/run_tests.py/filter.json/utils.py and sampled tests across c-testsuite and gcc-torture, identifying concrete feature demands (implicit decls, stdint typedefs, bit-fields, variadic macros, #pragma push/pop_macro, pointer casts) — systematic subset extraction before building.
Wrote a compiler_design.md plan and entered/exited plan mode; orientation from test sampling directly shaped the build/design order.

ABI details (16-byte stack alignment, rdi/rsi parameter passing, register-copy prologue) were recovered reactively during segfault debugging rather than probed upfront — the weak spot relative to the ABI clause of the higher anchors.
Derived standard C integer-promotion rules for shift/arithmetic/unary ops by analyzing failing test 00200 — mining failing tests to infer exact semantic requirements.

Compiled the failing case with real GCC to establish correct expected output and wrote numerous small repro cases (test_shift.c) plus assembly inspection to verify semantic assumptions against toolchain behavior.

dimensions.reasoning: Upfront orientation clearly meets the [8] anchor: the agent read run_tests.sh, sampled tests from each suite, and extracted a concrete language subset that shaped its design plan. Throughout the long horizon it sustained genuine research — deriving integer-promotion rules from failing tests and verifying assumptions against GCC output, small repros, and assembler/linker errors — which reaches toward [10]. But it did not probe ABI edge cases upfront (alignment/parameter passing were found reactively), and the research is largely per-failure whack-a-mole rather than anticipatory, so it falls short of 9-10; 8 is the best fit.

dimensions.name: Feature staging & milestone structure

evidence.note: Entered plan mode, surveyed tests to enumerate required features, wrote a compiler_design.md plan file, and produced a 'comprehensive implementation plan' with a clear pass structure — a genuine feature roadmap in dependency order.

Implementation was big-bang: a single delegated agent wrote ALL modules (lexer, preprocessor, ast, parser, type_checker, codegen, main) at once, rather than staging incremental feature milestones each with an explicit done-check.

Long reactive loop — fixes failing tests in roughly numeric file order (00051, 00063, 00107, 00121, 00162, 00197, 00200, 00207...), each followed by a full suite rerun. Ordering follows test numbers, not a dependency-aware milestone plan that targets features unlocking the most tests.
After reaching 100% on c_testsuite (146 tests), deliberately shifted focus to wacc failures — a coarse, data-driven milestone transition loosely tied to test subsets.
Tracked progress at the aggregate level (611/780, 78.3%) as the effective done-signal, rather than per-feature completion criteria.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent has a clear pass structure and a written feature roadmap in reasonable dependency order, and progress is genuinely tied to getting tests passing, with a coarse milestone shift from c_testsuite to wacc (anchor 5). It falls short of anchor 8 because the compiler was built big-bang rather than staged as fine-grained, dependency-sequenced feature milestones, and the subsequent work proceeds reactively in numeric test order with no per-feature test-subset done-signals defined in advance.

dimensions.name: Test-driven verification design

evidence.note: Disabled .s cleanup to keep generated assembly, compiled failing test 00020 in isolation, read the .s file, added debug prints in type_checker to trace variable resolution, fixed, then re-ran the single executable to confirm before the full suite — the core tight verification loop.

Compiled 00200.c with system GCC to obtain the known-correct expected output and debug prints, then diffed against its own compiler's behavior to localize a cast/type-promotion miscompile — direct comparison against a reference implementation (level-8 hallmark).

Wrote and repeatedly rewrote a minimal repro (/app/test_shift.c) varying sub-expressions (PTYPE macro, unsigned short, inline constants) to isolate exactly which construct diverged — minimal-reproduction discipline.

Segfault in 00207: read generated .s multiple times, attempted gdb/strace (unavailable), built fflush-instrumented repro to bisect which function crashed, then pinpointed pointer-truncation codegen bug — root-cause isolation distinguishing codegen from parser/sema.

After each fix rebuilt and re-ran the full 780-test suite to check pass count and catch regressions, tracking c_testsuite 100% then 611/780; regression detection was via full-suite reruns rather than an engineered subset/guard harness, keeping it below the level-10 anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent sustained a tight, self-correcting verification loop across the whole build: per-feature single-test isolation, assembly inspection, minimal repro programs, and explicit diffing against GCC known-correct output to determine which pass was miscompiling before editing — matching the level-8 anchor closely. It does not reach 10 because it built no categorized/scriptable subset runner or dedicated regression guards, relying on full-suite reruns for regression detection, so it sits solidly at 8.

dimensions.name: Pass-rate tracking & thrash detection

evidence.note: Re-runs the entire verification suite after nearly every fix ('observe the updated score'), maintaining a frequent whole-suite pulse rather than occasional counts.
Tracks failure-count trend numerically ('36 failed tests' -> 'down to 16'), showing awareness of movement, not just a single snapshot.

Reports per-suite pass rates (c_testsuite 100%/146, 77.1% overall; later 611/780, 78.3%) and uses the scoreboard to pivot from c_testsuite to wacc failures — category-level view and re-deriving next work.

Thrashes on test 00200 for a very long span, rewriting test_shift.c repeatedly (2691-2715) without bounding effort or moving on — failed thrash-detection, the opposite of anchor 8's stuck-recognition.
No explicit regression detection/attribution across the run; test scores are always read as forward progress, never checked for newly-broken previously-passing tests.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent keeps a genuine running tally — full-suite reruns after almost every change, numeric trend tracking (36->16), and per-suite pass breakdowns it uses to redirect effort — which matches anchor 5's 'running tally of pass counts by suite/feature.' However, it shows no explicit regression detection (weakening 5's second clause) and, most notably, fails anchor 8's thrash-bounding by looping on test 00200 for hundreds of steps with repeated repro rewrites instead of recognizing the stall and moving on. That combination places it right at level 5, not higher.

dimensions.name: Design revision under falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Discovered break was never implemented; reworked the affected component by adding a break_stack and threading it through switch/while/do-while/for, then rebuilt and re-verified — reworking rather than forcing the broken approach.
Changed the Stmt::Switch AST data structure (Vec<i64> -> Vec<(i64,String)>) when parser/codegen label mismatch caused linker errors; a data-structure revision with re-verification.

The same class of parser-vs-codegen label-naming bug recurred for switch break labels and was patched again by adding break_label as a fifth AST field — indicates a recurring class patched locally rather than solved structurally.

Added a promote_type helper and applied C standard integer-promotion rules across binary/unary operators when shift-type failures compounded — a moderately structural correction to the type system, re-verified against gcc output.
Handled VLA/non-constant array sizes with a 'default to 256' fallback — a workaround/hack rather than a structural fix, characteristic of symptom-level patching.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently reworks the affected component and re-verifies when an approach clearly fails (break_stack, switch label data structure, integer promotions), which matches anchor 5. However it stays below 8: it never recognizes an architectural limitation and executes a deliberate large refactor, the label-mismatch bug class recurs and is patched twice locally (1331-1351), and it leans on workarounds (VLA=256, float->int) without weighing refactor-vs-workaround or updating a design record. This places observed behavior squarely at the 5 anchor with slight symptom-patching pull toward 3.

dimensions.name: Compiler architecture & IR foresight

evidence.note: Upfront: plan doc enumerating types/structs/unions/typedefs, then clean modular separation (lexer/preprocessor/ast/parser/type_checker/codegen/main). AST designed as a TYPED AST with size/alignment and struct_defs, parser designed for typedef scoping — foresight beyond mere early-milestone adequacy.
Parser initialized all vars to Type::Int, so pointer sizing was wrong; needed flattening of multi-declaration compounds — type info was not properly threaded through the initial design.
Struct scoping not designed in; struct_scopes field and unique-tag helpers retrofitted onto Parser — a data-structure the initial model lacked.

Switch needed two structural AST changes: case labels -> Vec<(i64,String)>, then a 5th break_label field because parser and codegen disagreed on label naming — a broken inter-pass invariant, not a clean slot-in.
Local static variables forced adding current_function_name/local_static_mappings/global_static_vars to the Parser — significant retrofit for a contract feature.
Integer-promotion helper and post-op sized truncation added late in codegen/type_checker rather than being part of the original type model.

dimensions.reasoning: The initial architecture cleanly separates lexer/parser/sema/codegen and, unlike a bare level-5 design, includes a typed AST with a size/alignment/struct-layout model and typedef scoping that anticipate several hard features — pushing it above the level-5 anchor. However it falls short of level 8: cross-pass invariants were fragile (parser/codegen switch-label disagreement), and switch, struct scoping, and local statics required structural AST/parser retrofits rather than slotting in additively. This mix of real foresight in core representations plus meaningful painting-into-corners places it at 6.

rubric.task_read: This is an extreme long-horizon build: a from-scratch C compiler in Rust spanning lexer, full preprocessor, parser, semantic analysis, and x86-64 codegen, plus many advanced features (structs/unions, switch/case, typedef/casts, globals, short-circuit eval), gated by 780 tests across three real-world suites that must all pass. Difficulty comes from sheer scope, deep interdependence between passes, an implicit contract (C semantics + x86-64 ABI) the agent must recover, and the near-certainty that naive early design decisions will break under later features. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in every meta-work faculty — deep orientation, staged milestones tied to test subsets, relentless test-driven verification, accurate pass-rate tracking, and willingness to refactor architecture mid-flight.

dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI & test-suite orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding C language semantics, the x86-64 System V ABI/assembly conventions, and the structure/content of the three test suites before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The 'spec' is largely implicit — correct behavior is defined by C semantics, the calling convention, and what the 780 tests actually exercise. Acting without recovering this contract guarantees rework across nearly every pass.

anchors.0: Starts emitting code with no inspection of the test suites, run_tests.sh, or ABI conventions; guesses at behavior.
anchors.3: Skims run_tests.sh and writes a trivial hello-world compile; no systematic look at what features the tests demand or how the ABI/relocation works.
anchors.5: Reads run_tests.sh, samples tests from each suite, and establishes the basic x86-64 calling convention and assembly emission path before building core codegen.
anchors.8: Systematically categorizes tests by feature/difficulty, extracts the concrete language subset required, and probes ABI edge cases (struct passing, sizes/alignment, relocations) by compiling small reference cases; orientation directly shapes the build order.
anchors.10: Sustained, iterative research: continually mines failing tests to infer exact semantic requirements (integer promotion, evaluation order, layout rules), verifies assumptions against the assembler/linker behavior, and maintains a living understanding of the target contract that anticipates features before they are reached.

dimensions.name: Feature staging & milestone structure
dimensions.description: Breaking the compiler into an ordered hierarchy of passes and feature milestones, each with an explicit done-check (e.g. a passing test subset).
dimensions.why_it_matters: You cannot build all of C at once; the difference between steady progress and thrashing is a sane dependency-ordered plan (expressions before control flow before types before structs) with checkpoints.

anchors.0: No decomposition; attempts the whole compiler as one undifferentiated push or jumps between unrelated features at random.
anchors.3: Vague ordering ('do lexer, then parser, then codegen') with no feature-level milestones or explicit completion criteria.
anchors.5: Clear pass structure plus a feature roadmap in a reasonable dependency order, with milestones loosely tied to getting some tests passing.
anchors.8: Fine-grained, dependency-aware milestones each bound to a concrete test subset as its done-signal, sequenced so each milestone builds on verified prior ones; ordering reflects which features unlock the most tests.
anchors.10: A living milestone hierarchy that is re-prioritized as data arrives — smallest-viable-slice ordering, explicit gating criteria per milestone, and deliberate deferral of hard/rare features until foundations are proven, sustained coherently across the whole horizon.

dimensions.name: Test-driven verification design
dimensions.description: Deliberately building/using checks — incremental runs of test subsets, minimal repro cases, diffing against expected behavior — rather than assuming generated code is correct.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With 780 opaque pass/fail tests and a compiler where any pass can silently miscompile, a disciplined verification loop is the only way to know progress is real and to localize defects.

anchors.0: Never runs the tests until the very end, or writes code with no way to confirm correctness; assumes success.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally as the only check; no isolation of failures, no smaller probes.
anchors.5: Runs relevant test subsets after each feature and uses the pass/fail signal to guide fixes.
anchors.8: Builds a tight loop: reduces failing tests to minimal reproductions, inspects generated assembly, and compares against known-correct output to pinpoint which pass is wrong before editing.
anchors.10: Engineers verification infrastructure beyond what's handed over — categorized/scriptable subset runs, regression guards so fixed tests stay fixed, and root-cause isolation that distinguishes lexer/parser/sema/codegen defects — sustaining fast, trustworthy signal across the entire build.

dimensions.name: Pass-rate tracking & thrash detection
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate done-vs-remaining picture (which tests/features pass), and detecting regressions, circular debugging, or stalls across a very long horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Over hundreds of features and edits, it is easy to lose the plot, regress previously-passing tests, or loop on one stubborn failure; an accurate live picture is what sustains net forward motion.

anchors.0: No sense of how many tests pass or which features remain; edits blindly with no scoreboard.
anchors.3: Occasional whole-suite counts but no tracking of trends, regressions, or which categories are outstanding.
anchors.5: Keeps a running tally of pass counts by suite/feature and notices when a change breaks previously-passing tests.
anchors.8: Maintains a structured, current view of pass rate by category and remaining work, and recognizes when stuck on one test — bounding effort and moving on rather than looping.
anchors.10: Treats pass-rate as a managed signal: detects regressions immediately and attributes them, spots circular/thrashing debugging early and deliberately changes tactics, and continuously re-derives the highest-leverage remaining work from the scoreboard.

dimensions.name: Design revision under falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising architecture, data structures, or approach when a later feature (types, structs, ABI detail) exposes that an earlier design cannot support it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Compilers are notorious for early choices (untyped AST, ad-hoc register allocation, string-based codegen) that collapse under types/structs; the ability to recognize and refactor rather than pile hacks decides whether the tail of the task is reachable.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on a broken design, piling special-cases and hacks even as failures compound.
anchors.3: Patches symptoms locally; resists structural change even when the same class of bug keeps recurring.
anchors.5: When an approach clearly fails, reworks the affected component and re-verifies rather than forcing it.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a limitation is architectural (not local), makes a deliberate refactor (e.g. adding type info through the AST/IR), and confirms the change unblocks the stuck feature class.
anchors.10: Proactively detects design strain before it becomes a wall, weighs refactor-vs-workaround explicitly, executes larger restructurings cleanly while protecting already-passing tests, and updates the plan/design record so the correction propagates instead of recurring.

dimensions.name: Compiler architecture & IR foresight
dimensions.description: Choosing pass boundaries and core data structures (AST/IR, symbol tables, type representation) with enough foresight to accommodate the full required feature set rather than painting into a corner.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Unlike generic decomposition (what to do when) or adaptation (fixing after breakage), this is the upfront design judgment specific to compilers: a representation that anticipates types, structs, and the ABI avoids the most expensive class of rework on this task.

anchors.0: No deliberate architecture; monolithic, ad-hoc string-munging with no separable passes or reusable structures.
anchors.3: Minimal structure that works for the first trivial cases but has no provision for types, scopes, or layout.
anchors.5: Clean separation of lexer/parser/sema/codegen with data structures adequate for the early feature milestones.
anchors.8: Core representations (typed AST/IR, symbol/scope tables, type/layout model) are designed with the later hard features in mind, so structs/typedef/switch slot in without wholesale rewrites.
anchors.10: Architecture demonstrably anticipates the full contract — extensible IR and type system, clear invariants between passes — enabling most advanced features to be added additively; foresight is evidenced by later features landing cleanly rather than by luck.
